result.summary: This PR refactors the wallet's SQLite backend to wrap raw sqlite3_stmt pointers in a new SQLiteStatement RAII class, replacing manual sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_finalize/sqlite3_reset calls with constructor/destructor and member functions (Bind, Step, Reset, Column). It also changes statement lifecycle so per-batch prepared statements are constructed lazily on first use rather than all at once. The author states this is groundwork for future work using more complex SQL statements, referencing the follow-up PR #33034 which stores transactions in a separate table.
result.problem: The existing sqlite.cpp code manages raw sqlite3_stmt objects manually across many functions, which the author and reviewers agree is error-prone and harder to extend for more complex statements needed by upcoming wallet work (transaction storage refactor in #33034).

result.card: This PR refactors bitcoind's wallet SQLite backend (src/wallet/sqlite.cpp/.h) to wrap raw sqlite3_stmt handles in a new SQLiteStatement RAII class, replacing scattered manual prepare/finalize/reset calls with constructor/destructor management and member functions. The author's stated motivation is to make the code easier to extend for more complex SQL statements, explicitly citing the follow-up PR #33034 (storing transactions in a separate SQLite table) as the beneficiary. It is purely an internal maintainability change with no direct user-facing benefit, though a few incidental error-handling behavior changes (exceptions replacing optional returns, a constructor that can now throw where a function used to return nullptr) were surfaced and mostly resolved across extensive review by vasild, pablomartin4btc, davidgumberg, and Eunovo. vasild and pablomartin4btc gave ACKs; no reviewer opposes the change, though some ACKs are marked stale after later force-pushes. The author has continued actively addressing nits through August 2026, and no rebase or CI issue blocks review.
